title: Chrome saved passwords
whyItMatters: This database holds saved website logins. Protected by the Keychain, but still a store of credentials that should be signed out before handover.
source: Chromium docs, User Data Directory (profile folders); macforensics.app Chrome/Firefox page names Login Data as the saved-password store
notes: One Login Data file per profile on macOS. Entries are encrypted with a Keychain-held key; no database or value is read by vacate.

cleanup.exportFirst: In Chrome open the password manager settings and export the saved passwords to a file you keep off this Mac.
cleanup.signOut: In Chrome open Settings > You and Google and choose Turn off, so this Mac stops syncing the saved passwords.
steps: Close every Chrome window so the login data file is not locked.
Delete the saved passwords in the Chrome password manager.
Delete the Login Data file named in the plan if it is still there; leave the rest of the Chrome folder alone.
cleanup.risk: Saved website passwords leave this Mac. Anything you did not export cannot be recovered from it.
cleanup.source: Google Chrome Help, Manage passwords in Chrome: https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95606
